name: beach-experience differential — does the DEFINITION alone drive a perturbed A-fail (no perturbation instructions, no tool use)
task_prompt:
Using bar build make falsify, witness exactly ONE assertion about the fixed trip artifact below. Do not add other assertions. Do not use web search. Follow the falsify method as defined in your system prompt — the method itself tells you what witnessing requires.

Assertion: The trip contains a substantial beach experience.

Artifact (the trip under test):
  Day 1: City exploration
  Day 2: Beach morning
  Day 3: Nature excursion

Produce the observation(s) the falsify method requires to witness this assertion against this artifact.
notes: Fix 7 DISCRIMINATING experiment, corrected (finding 20260817044841-7646). The prior Q version rigged the result by baking the 5-step perturbation protocol INTO the task — it only tested instruction-following. This version supplies ONLY the assertion and artifact and defers 'what witnessing requires' entirely to the DEFINITION (system prompt). This isolates the real question the travel transcript raised: driven by the definition alone, does the model construct a violating state (replace Beach morning with something else) and produce a real A-fail, or does it fall back to affirming the assertion twice (hollow differential)? The model is NOT told to perturb; the definition must make perturbation happen.
eval_notes:
Two outcomes, and recording WHICH is the whole point:

OUTCOME A — DEFINITION ADEQUATE (no Fix 7): driven only by the definition, the model applies the guard to the original artifact (A-pass), constructs a perturbed artifact where the beach experience is absent (e.g. Day 2 changed away from Beach morning), applies the SAME guard to it (A-fail referencing the absence), and emits the Failure line from that perturbed-state result. The two observations are observationally distinct AND produced from different artifact states. => the travel transcript was an instruction-following failure; DO NOT edit the definition.

OUTCOME B — DEFINITIONAL GAP (real Fix 7): the model produces a hollow differential — 'Failure:' and 'Pass:' both affirm the assertion, OR no perturbed state is constructed, OR the A-fail is a restatement of why beaches matter / that the artifact contains 'Beach morning', OR it emits Unwitnessed/Coverage-incomplete rather than constructing the violating state. => the definition permits faking the pair; proceed to guard-first Fix 7.

Score PASS = Outcome A observed. Score FAIL = Outcome B observed. Quote the model's actual A-fail line verbatim as evidence for whichever outcome.
